title: mlflow top-level API exports: a new public mlflow.* function needs an import, an __all__ entry, and an api_inventory.txt line
answers: How do I make a new tracking function available as mlflow.something at the top level?
Why does my new fluent function not show up in the mlflow namespace or in the API reference inventory?
Where are the public mlflow.* names exported and listed?
I added a new fluent wrapper to mlflow/tracking/fluent.py; what else must change for it to be public?
body:
Path: mlflow/__init__.py:__all__ re-exports the fluent tracking functions from mlflow/tracking/fluent.py (run, log_*, delete_*, search_*, etc.) so they are callable as mlflow.<name>; docs/api_reference/api_inventory.txt lists every public mlflow.* name for the API reference.
Rule: A new public fluent function in mlflow/tracking/fluent.py:<function name> is exposed by three coordinated edits: add it to the `from mlflow.tracking.fluent import (...)` block in mlflow/__init__.py, add its string to `__all__` in mlflow/__init__.py, and add the dotted name (mlflow.<name>) in sorted position in docs/api_reference/api_inventory.txt. Keep the list in the same order the neighbouring entries use.
Constraints: Applies to public functions meant for users. Private helpers (leading underscore) and client-only methods on MlflowClient do not need these edits. The inventory file is auto-generated, so regenerating it (e.g. via the autoformat tooling) is preferable to hand-editing when available; the diff hand-inserted the two new lines.
applies: Adding any new public top-level mlflow.* function that is re-exported from a submodule such as mlflow/tracking/fluent.py.
says: A newly released tracking function cannot be imported directly from the root library.
The restore run feature is missing from the published API reference documentation.
Make newly added experiment restoration methods accessible directly from the main package.
New tracking commands fail to appear in the official reference inventory list.
search: Exporting a new public fluent function from `mlflow/tracking/fluent.py` requires importing it in `mlflow/__init__.py`, adding its name to `__all__`, and adding the dotted entry in sorted order to `docs/api_reference/api_inventory.txt`. Applies to public top-level `mlflow.*` functions meant for users, such as `restore_experiment` and `restore_run`. Private helpers with leading underscores and client-only methods on `MlflowClient` are excluded from these requirements.
